readings.title: Conquests of Yehudah
readings.subtitle: Successes in the South
readings.text: [Judges 1:1] And it came to be after the death of Yehoshua, that the children of Yisra’el asked <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, saying, “Who of us shall go up first against the Kena‘anites to fight against them?” [2] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> said, <dq>“Yehudah shall go up. See, <dn>I</dn> have given the land into his hand.”</dq> [3] And Yehudah said to Shim‘on his brother, “Come up with me to my allotted inheritance, and let us fight against the Kena‘anites, and I myself shall go with you to your allotted inheritance.” So Shim‘on went with him. [4] And Yehudah went up, and <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> gave the Kena‘anites and the Perizzites into their hand, and they smote them in Bezeq, ten thousand men. [5] And they found Aḏoni-Bezeq in Bezeq, and fought against him, and smote the Kena‘anites and the Perizzites. [6] And Aḏoni-Bezeq fled, and they pursued him and caught him and cut off his thumbs and big toes. [7] And Aḏoni-Bezeq said, “Seventy sovereigns with their thumbs and big toes cut off used to gather scraps under my table. As I have done, so <dn>Elohim</dn> has repaid me.” And they brought him to Yerushalayim, and there he died. [8] And the children of Yehudah fought against Yerushalayim and captured it, and they smote it with the edge of the sword and set the city on fire. [9] And afterward the children of Yehudah went down to fight against the Kena‘anites who dwelt in the mountains, and in the South, and in the low country. [10] And Yehudah went against the Kena‘anites who dwelt in Ḥeḇron – now the name of Ḥeḇron was formerly Qiryath Arḇa – and they smote Shĕshay, and Aḥiman, and Talmay. [11] And from there he went against the inhabitants of Deḇir – now the name of Deḇir was formerly Qiryath Sĕpher. [12] And Kalĕḇ said, “He who smites Qiryath Sĕpher and captures it, to him I shall give my daughter Aḵsah as wife.” [13] And Othni’ĕl son of Qenaz, Kalĕḇ’s younger brother, captured it, so he gave him his daughter Aḵsah as wife. [14] And it came to be, when she came to him, that she urged him to ask her father for a field. And she dismounted from her donkey, and Kalĕḇ said to her, “What is the matter?” [15] And she said to him, “Give me a blessing. Since you have given me land in the South, give me also springs of water.” So Kalĕḇ gave her the upper springs and the lower springs. [16] And the children of the Qĕnite, father-in-law of Mosheh, went up from the City of Palms with the children of Yehudah into the Wilderness of Yehudah, which is in the South of Arad, and they went and dwelt among the people. [17] And Yehudah went with his brother Shim‘on, and they smote the Kena‘anites who inhabited Tsephath, and put it under the ban. So the name of the city was called Ḥormah. [18] And Yehudah captured Azzah with its border, and Ashqelon with its border, and Eqron with its border.

readings.title: Incomplete Conquests
readings.subtitle: The Nations That Remained
readings.text: [Judges 1:19] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> was with Yehudah, and they took possession of the mountains, but they could not drive out the inhabitants of the valley, because they had chariots of iron. [20] And they gave Ḥeḇron to Kalĕḇ, as Mosheh had said. And he drove out from there the three sons of Anaq. [21] But the children of Binyamin did not drive out the Yeḇusites who inhabited Yerushalayim, so the Yeḇusites have dwelt with the children of Binyamin in Yerushalayim to this day. [22] And the house of Yoseph also went up against Bĕyth Ěl, and <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> was with them. [23] And the house of Yoseph sent men to spy out Bĕyth Ěl – now the name of the city was formerly Luz. [24] And the spies saw a man coming out of the city, and they said to him, “Please show us the entrance to the city, and we shall show you loving-commitment.” [25] And he showed them the entrance to the city, and they smote the city with the edge of the sword, but they let the man and all his clan go. [26] And the man went to the land of the Ḥittites, and built a city, and called its name Luz, which is its name to this day. [27] And Menashsheh did not dispossess Bĕyth She’an and its villages, nor Ta‘anaḵ and its villages, nor the inhabitants of Dor and its villages, nor the inhabitants of Yiḇle‘am and its villages, nor the inhabitants of Megiddo and its villages, for the Kena‘anites desired to dwell in that land. [28] And it came to be, when Yisra’el was strong, that they put the Kena‘anites to compulsory labour, but did not utterly drive them out. [29] And Ephrayim did not drive out the Kena‘anites who dwelt in Gezer, so the Kena‘anites dwelt among them in Gezer. [30] Zebulun did not drive out the inhabitants of Qitron, nor the inhabitants of Nahalal, so the Kena‘anites dwelt among them, and became subject to compulsory labour. [31] Asher did not drive out the inhabitants of Akko, nor the inhabitants of Tsiḏon, nor of Aḥlaḇ, nor of Aḵziḇ, nor of Ḥelbah, nor of Aphiq, nor of Reḥoḇ. [32] So the Asherites dwelt among the Kena‘anites, the inhabitants of the land, for they did not drive them out. [33] Naphtali did not drive out the inhabitants of Bĕyth Shemesh, nor the inhabitants of Bĕyth Anath, but dwelt among the Kena‘anites, the inhabitants of the land. And the inhabitants of Bĕyth Shemesh and of Bĕyth Anath became subject to compulsory labour for them. [34] And the Amorites pressed the children of Dan into the mountains, for they would not allow them to come down to the valley. [35] And the Amorites desired to dwell in Mount Ḥeres, in Ayalon, and in Sha‘albim. But the hand of the house of Yoseph became heavy, so that they became subject to compulsory labour. [36] And the border of the Amorites was from the Ascent of Aqrabbim, from Sela and upward.

readings.title: The Angel at Bokim
readings.subtitle: A Covenant Broken
readings.text: [Judges 2:1] And the Messenger of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> came up from Gilgal to Bokim, and said, <dq>“<dn>I</dn> led you up from Mitsrayim and brought you to the land of which <dn>I</dn> swore to your fathers, and <dn>I</dn> said, ‘<dn>I</dn> do not break <dn>My</dn> covenant with you,</dq> [2] <dq>and you do not make a covenant with the inhabitants of this land – break down their altars.’ But you have not obeyed <dn>My</dn> voice. What is this you have done?</dq> [3] <dq>“Therefore <dn>I</dn> also said, ‘<dn>I</dn> do not drive them out before you, and they shall be adversaries to you, and their mighty ones shall be a snare to you.’ ”</dq> [4] And it came to be, when the Messenger of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> spoke these words to all the children of Yisra’el, that the people lifted up their voice and wept. [5] So they called the name of that place Bokim, and slaughtered there to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.

readings.title: A Generation Arises
readings.subtitle: The Death of Joshua Recounted
readings.text: [Judges 2:6] And Yehoshua sent the people away, and the children of Yisra’el went each to his own inheritance to possess the land. [7] And the people served <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> all the days of Yehoshua, and all the days of the elders who outlived Yehoshua, who had seen all the great works of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> which <dn>He</dn> had done for Yisra’el. [8] And Yehoshua son of Nun, the servant of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, died, being one hundred and ten years old. [9] And they buried him within the border of his inheritance in Timnath Ḥeres, in the mountains of Ephrayim, on the north side of Mount Ga‘ash.

readings.title: The Great Apostasy
readings.subtitle: Abandoning YeHoVaH
readings.text: [Judges 2:10] And all that generation were likewise gathered to their fathers, and another generation arose after them who did not know <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> nor the work which <dn>He</dn> had done for Yisra’el. [11] And the children of Yisra’el did evil in the eyes of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, and served the Ba‘als, [12] and forsook <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> <dn>Elohim</dn> of their fathers, who had brought them out of the land of Mitsrayim, and went after other mighty ones, of the mighty ones of the people who were all around them, and bowed down to them, and provoked <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. [13] So they forsook <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> and served Ba‘al and the Ashtoreths. [14] And the displeasure of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> burned against Yisra’el, and <dn>He</dn> gave them into the hand of plunderers who plundered them. And <dn>He</dn> sold them into the hands of their enemies round about, so that they were unable to stand before their enemies any longer. [15] Wherever they went out, the hand of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> was against them for evil, as <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> had spoken, and as <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> had sworn to them. And they were greatly distressed.

readings.title: The Cycle of Judges
readings.subtitle: Rebellion, Ruin, Repentance, Rescue
readings.text: [Judges 2:16] Then <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> raised up rulers, and they saved them from the hand of those who plundered them. [17] However, they did not listen to their rulers either, but went whoring after other mighty ones, and bowed down to them. They turned aside quickly from the way in which their fathers walked, in obeying the commands of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> – they did not do so. [18] And when <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> raised up rulers for them, <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> was with the ruler and saved them from the hand of their enemies all the days of the ruler, for <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> relented because of their groaning before those who oppressed them and crushed them. [19] And it came to be, when the ruler was dead, that they would turn back and do more corruptly than their fathers, to go after other mighty ones, to serve them and bow down to them. They did not refrain from their practices and from their stubborn way. [20] And the displeasure of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> burned against Yisra’el, and <dn>He</dn> said, <dq>“Because this nation has transgressed <dn>My</dn> covenant which <dn>I</dn> commanded their fathers, and has not obeyed <dn>My</dn> voice,</dq> [21] <dq><dn>I</dn> also shall no longer drive out before them any of the nations which Yehoshua left when he died,</dq> [22] <dq>in order to try Yisra’el by them, whether they guard the way of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> to walk in them as their fathers guarded them, or not.”</dq> [23] So <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> left those nations, without driving them out immediately, and did not give them into the hand of Yehoshua.

readings.title: Training for War
readings.subtitle: The Nations Left to Test Israel
readings.text: [Judges 3:1] Now these are the nations which <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> left, to try Yisra’el by them, all of them who had not known all the battles of Kena‘an, [2] only that the generations of the children of Yisra’el might know, to teach them battle, only those who had not known it before: [3] five masters of the Philistines, and all the Kena‘anites, and the Tsiḏonians, and the Ḥiwites who dwelt in Mount Leḇanon, from Mount Ba‘al Ḥermon to the entrance of Ḥamath. [4] And they were left to be a test for Yisra’el by them, to know whether they obeyed the commands of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, which <dn>He</dn> had commanded their fathers by the hand of Mosheh. [5] Thus the children of Yisra’el dwelt in the midst of the Kena‘anites, the Ḥittites, and the Amorites, and the Perizzites, and the Ḥiwites, and the Yeḇusites. [6] And they took their daughters to be their wives, and gave their daughters to their sons, and served their mighty ones.

readings.title: Othniel: The Lion of God
readings.subtitle: The First Deliverer
readings.text: [Judges 3:7] And the children of Yisra’el did evil in the eyes of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, and forgot <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> their <dn>Elohim</dn>, and served the Ba‘als and the Asheroth. [8] And the displeasure of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> burned against Yisra’el, and <dn>He</dn> sold them into the hand of Kushan-Rish‘athayim sovereign of Aram Naharayim. And the children of Yisra’el served Kushan-Rish‘athayim eight years. [9] And the children of Yisra’el cried out to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, and <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> raised up a saviour for the children of Yisra’el, who saved them: Othni’ĕl son of Qenaz, Kalĕḇ’s younger brother. [10] And the Spirit of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> came upon him, and he ruled Yisra’el, and went out to battle. And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> gave Kushan-Rish‘athayim sovereign of Aram into his hand, and his hand prevailed over Kushan-Rish‘athayim. [11] And the land had rest for forty years. Then Othni’ĕl son of Qenaz died.

readings.title: Ehud: The Left-Handed Savior
readings.subtitle: Defeating the Fat King of Moab
readings.text: [Judges 3:12] And the children of Yisra’el again did evil in the eyes of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> made Eg̱lon sovereign of Mo’aḇ strong against Yisra’el, because they had done evil in the eyes of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. [13] And he gathered to himself the children of Ammon and Amalĕq, and went and smote Yisra’el, and they took possession of the City of Palms. [14] And the children of Yisra’el served Eg̱lon sovereign of Mo’aḇ eighteen years. [15] And the children of Yisra’el cried out to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, and <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> raised up a saviour for them: Ěhuḏ son of Gĕra, the Binyamite, a left-handed man. And by him the children of Yisra’el sent a present to Eg̱lon sovereign of Mo’aḇ. [16] And Ěhuḏ made himself a sword, double-edged, a cubit in length, and fastened it under his garments on his right thigh. [17] And he brought the present to Eg̱lon sovereign of Mo’aḇ. Now Eg̱lon was a very fat man. [18] And it came to be, when he had ended presenting the present, that he sent away the people who had carried the present. [19] But he himself turned back from the stone images that were at Gilgal, and said, “I have a secret word for you, O sovereign.” And he said, “Silence!” And all who attended him went out from him. [20] And Ěhuḏ came to him, now he was sitting upstairs in his cool private room. And Ěhuḏ said, “I have a word from <dn>Elohim</dn> for you.” And he stood up from his seat. [21] And Ěhuḏ reached with his left hand, took the sword from his right thigh, and thrust it into his belly. [22] And the handle also went in after the blade, and the fat closed over the blade, for he did not draw the sword out of his belly, and his entrails came out. [23] And Ěhuḏ went out through the porch and shut the doors of the upper room behind him and locked them. [24] And when he had gone out, the servants came to look, and saw that the doors of the upper room were locked. So they said, “He is only covering his feet in the cool room.” [25] And they waited till they were ashamed, but look, he did not open the doors of the upper room. So they took the key and opened them, and saw their master fallen down dead on the floor. [26] And Ěhuḏ escaped while they delayed, and passed beyond the stone images and escaped to Se‘irah. [27] And it came to be, when he arrived, that he blew the shophar in the mountains of Ephrayim, and the children of Yisra’el went down with him from the mountains, and he led them. [28] And he said to them, “Follow me, for <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has given your enemies the Mo’aḇites into your hand.” And they went down after him, and seized the fords of the Yardĕn leading to Mo’aḇ, and did not allow anyone to pass over. [29] And at that time they smote about ten thousand men of Mo’aḇ, all stout men of valour, and not a man escaped. [30] So Mo’aḇ was humbled that day under the hand of Yisra’el. And the land had rest for eighty years.
